usage: trading_assistant.cli [-h] [--short SHORT] [--long LONG]
                             [--rsi-period RSI_PERIOD] [--backtest]
                             [--cash AMOUNT] [--fee AMOUNT] [--fee-pct PCT]
                             [--slippage PCT] [--position-size FRACTION]
                             [--stop-loss PCT] [--take-profit PCT]
                             [--export FILE] [--fill {close,open}]
                             [--resample {weekly,monthly}]
                             [--strategy {sma_cross,rsi_reversion,breakout,ema_cross,momentum,zscore_reversion,hull_trend}]
                             [--param KEY=VALUE] [--stats] [--config FILE]
                             [--json] [--chart] [--candles] [--scan FOLDER]
                             [--min-score N] [--top N] [--report FILE]
                             csv_path

Suggest BUY/SELL/HOLD from closing prices.

positional arguments:
  csv_path              CSV file with a 'close' column

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --short SHORT         short SMA window (default: 20)
  --long LONG           long SMA window (default: 50)
  --rsi-period RSI_PERIOD
                        RSI lookback (default: 14)
  --backtest            also simulate trading the crossover signal over the
                        whole file
  --cash AMOUNT         starting cash for --backtest (default: 10,000)
  --fee AMOUNT          fixed cost charged on every buy and every sell in
                        --backtest (default: 0)
  --fee-pct PCT         percentage of traded value charged on every buy and
                        sell in --backtest, e.g. 0.1 for 0.1% (default: 0)
  --slippage PCT        with --backtest, buys fill this percentage above and
                        sells this percentage below the fill price, before
                        fees, e.g. 0.1 for 0.1% (default: 0)
  --position-size FRACTION
                        with --backtest, each buy spends at most this fraction
                        of the account value (above 0, at most 1), costs and
                        slippage included (default: all the cash)
  --stop-loss PCT       with --backtest, sell when a bar's low reaches the
                        entry price less PCT% (reads a candle file; cannot be
                        combined with --resample yet)
  --take-profit PCT     with --backtest, sell when a bar's high reaches the
                        entry price plus PCT% (reads a candle file; cannot be
                        combined with --resample yet); if a bar touches both
                        levels the stop wins
  --trailing-stop PCT   with --backtest, sell when a bar's low reaches the
                        highest high since entry less PCT% (the bar's own high
                        is not used; reads a candle file; cannot be combined
                        with --resample yet); works next to --stop-loss and
                        --take-profit: the higher of the stop and trail levels
                        is used, and it wins over the target if a bar touches
                        both
  --risk-pct PCT        with --backtest, size each buy by risk: PCT% of the
                        account value (above 0, at most 100) divided by a stop
                        distance of --atr-mult times the ATR (--atr-period
                        bars) on the bar the buy signal came on, rounded down
                        to whole shares; with --position-size the smaller size
                        wins. A buy that gets 0 shares this way (no ATR yet,
                        or under one share) is skipped and counted in the
                        report. This only sets the number of shares: no stop
                        is placed, so a loss is not limited to PCT% (--atr-
                        stop adds a stop at the distance of the buy that
                        opened the position; even then a gap, slippage, fees
                        or a later buy into the position can lose more). Works
                        next to --stop-loss, --take-profit and --trailing-
                        stop, and next to --atr-stop (reads a candle file;
                        cannot be combined with --resample yet)
  --atr-mult N          with --risk-pct, the stop distance used for sizing is
                        N times the ATR (above 0; default: 2); without --atr-
                        stop it only sets the number of shares, no stop is
                        placed. With --atr-stop (with or without --risk-pct)
                        it is the distance of the ATR stop, taken on the buy
                        that opened the position
  --atr-period N        with --risk-pct, the number of bars in the ATR (a
                        whole number of at least 1; default: 14); --atr-stop
                        uses the same ATR
  --atr-stop            with --backtest, sell when a bar's low reaches the
                        entry price less --atr-mult times the ATR (--atr-
                        period bars) on the bar the buy signal came on; that
                        distance is fixed when the position opens, and a later
                        buy moves the level with the average entry price only.
                        A buy signal with no ATR yet (or an ATR of 0) is
                        skipped and counted in the report. Works next to
                        --stop-loss, --trailing-stop and --take-profit: the
                        highest stop level is used (on a tie the stop, then
                        the trail, then atr) and it wins over the target if a
                        bar touches both; its fills say atr. With --risk-pct a
                        position's first buy is sized on the same distance the
                        stop uses; a gap, slippage, fees or a later buy (sized
                        on its own signal bar's ATR) can still lose more than
                        the risk (reads a candle file; cannot be combined with
                        --resample yet)
  --cooldown N          with --backtest and one of --stop-loss, --trailing-
                        stop or --atr-stop: after a sell by one of them, no
                        buy can fill for the next N bars (a whole number of at
                        least 1). A buy due then is dropped, not delayed, and
                        counted in the report. A --take-profit or signal sell
                        starts no cooldown
  --min-hold N          with --backtest, drop a signal sell due before the
                        position has been held N bars (a whole number of at
                        least 1), counted from the buy that opened it; a later
                        buy does not restart the count. The sell is dropped,
                        not delayed, and counted in the report. Stops, the
                        target, --max-hold and --max-drawdown still sell
                        inside the window. Needs no stop and works with a
                        close-only file and with --resample (N counts the
                        resampled bars)
  --max-hold N          with --backtest, sell the whole position N bars after
                        the buy that opened it (a whole number of at least 1),
                        at that bar's fill price (close, or open with --fill
                        open); a later buy does not restart the count. A bar
                        that already has a fill keeps it and the sale waits
                        for the next bar. Its fills say time; it starts no
                        cooldown. Needs no stop and works with a close-only
                        file and with --resample (N counts the resampled bars)
  --max-drawdown PCT    with --backtest, halt when the account value at a
                        close is PCT% or more below its highest value at a
                        close so far (above 0, below 100): from the next bar
                        on no buy can fill (each buy due is dropped and
                        counted in the report), and a position still held is
                        sold on the next bar at its fill price (close, or open
                        with --fill open). A signal, stop, trail, ATR stop,
                        target or time sale on that bar goes first and keeps
                        its reason; otherwise the fill says drawdown. It
                        starts no cooldown. Needs no stop and works with a
                        close-only file and with --resample
  --breakeven PCT       with --backtest, once the high of a bar after the
                        entry bar is at or above the entry price (the average
                        price paid) plus PCT% (above 0), sell on a later bar
                        whose low reaches the entry price (at that price, or
                        at the bar's open if it opens at or below it); no
                        allowance is made for fees or slippage. A later buy
                        moves the level with the average price. Works next to
                        --stop-loss, --trailing-stop and --atr-stop (the
                        highest stop level is used; on a tie the stop, then
                        the trail, then atr, then breakeven) and wins over
                        --take-profit if a bar touches both; at or above
                        --take-profit it can never act, unless a later buy
                        into the position moves the average (a lower-priced
                        one with close fills, any one with --fill open). Its
                        fills say breakeven. It counts as a stop for
                        --cooldown: --cooldown may be used with it alone, and
                        a breakeven sale starts the cooldown (reads a candle
                        file; cannot be combined with --resample yet)
  --max-losses N        with --backtest, after N losing round trips in a row
                        (a whole number of at least 1) no buy can fill for the
                        rest of the run; each buy due then is dropped and
                        counted in the report. A round trip loses when its
                        profit after costs is below 0; any other, one at
                        exactly 0.00 included, resets the count. Nothing is
                        held when the halt starts, so nothing is sold because
                        of it. Needs no stop and works with a close-only file
                        and with --resample
  --scale-out PCT       with --backtest, sell half the shares held (rounded
                        down) once per position when the high of a bar after
                        the entry bar reaches the entry price (the average
                        cost of the shares held) plus PCT% (above 0): at that
                        price, or at the bar's open if it opens at or above
                        it. The rest stays open. Any other fill on the bar
                        goes first and the scale-out is skipped on that bar;
                        with close fills a --max-hold or --max-drawdown sale
                        waits for it. A partial sale is not a round trip: its
                        proceeds count in the round trip the rest completes.
                        Its fills say scale_out. It starts no cooldown, --min-
                        hold does not hold it back, and it needs no other exit
                        option (reads a candle file; cannot be combined with
                        --resample yet)
  --export FILE         with --backtest, write one CSV row per bar (account
                        value, signal, fills) to FILE
  --fill {close,open}   with --backtest, the price of the next bar a signal is
                        filled at (default: close); open reads the file as a
                        candle file and cannot be combined with --resample yet
  --resample {weekly,monthly}
                        reduce daily bars to weekly or monthly bars before
                        analysing (needs a 'date' column)
  --strategy {sma_cross,rsi_reversion,breakout,ema_cross,momentum,zscore_reversion,hull_trend}
                        rule traded by --backtest (default: sma_cross); does
                        not change the Signal line
  --param KEY=VALUE     override a strategy parameter in --backtest, e.g.
                        window=10 (repeatable)
  --stats               with --backtest, also print the risk and return
                        statistics block
  --trade-list          with --backtest, print one row per completed round
                        trip after the report (after the risk and return block
                        with --stats, before --chart): entry bar, exit bar,
                        bars held, shares bought, outlay, proceeds, P/L,
                        return % and the reason of the sale that completed it,
                        plus a row for a position still held at the end
                        (unrealized: marked at the last close, no selling
                        costs). Its footer repeats the Round trips numbers.
                        Needs no candle file and works with --resample; with
                        --json the backtest object gets a trade_list array
                        instead
  --config FILE         read defaults from an INI file; flags win over the
                        file (no file is read unless this is given or
                        $TRADING_ASSISTANT_CONFIG is set)
  --json                print the report as one JSON object on stdout instead
                        of text (cannot be combined with --chart)
  --chart               print a text chart of the closes after the report
                        (fills marked B and S with --backtest)
  --explain             print one sentence right after the Signal line
                        explaining it: the decision, the --short and --long
                        SMA on the last bar and on the bar before, and why
                        (always the SMA crossover, whatever --strategy is;
                        needs no candle file; cannot be combined with --scan)
  --candles             read the file as a candle file (date, open, high, low,
                        close, volume) and analyse its closes; cannot be
                        combined with --resample yet
  --scan FOLDER         instead of one price file, give the combined score of
                        every .csv file directly inside FOLDER (cannot be
                        combined with a price file or backtest options)
  --min-score N         with --scan, keep only the files scoring N or more
  --top N               with --scan, show only the first N rows (after --min-
                        score)
  --report FILE         with --scan, also write a Markdown report to FILE (the
                        screen output does not change)

Research aid only. Not financial advice.
